title: Maximum Depth of a Binary Tree
description:
The depth of a binary tree is the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf. Find the depth of the given tree (an empty tree has depth 0).

Input format
One line: the tree in level-order, values separated by spaces, with the word null for a missing child. Children of null nodes are not listed (the usual level-order serialisation). For example "3 9 20 null null 15 7".

Output format
One integer: the depth of the tree.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes <= 100000. Values are integers. An empty tree is written as the single token null.
hints: The depth of a tree is 1 plus the larger depth of its two sub-trees. What is the depth of an empty tree?
Write a recursive function depth(node) = 0 if node is empty, otherwise 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).
For very deep trees recursion can overflow the stack; a breadth-first traversal that counts levels needs no recursion.

examples.explanation: The tree is a chain of two nodes.
